concepts.quote: if (value == 1) result = 30; elif (value == 2 || value == 3) result = -10; else result = 5;
concepts.why: The answer correctly turns the switch into an else-if chain whose final else plays the role of default, but `elif` is Python, not Java. Java needs `else if`, so this code would not compile.
It writes a valid braceless if with a boolean condition, but does not trace it or explain why it works.
It correctly joins two comparisons with || into one boolean condition that covers the fall-through from case 2 to case 3.
The answer says nothing about short-circuit evaluation.
